skill.name: image-edit
skill.description: Image editing for agents: image-to-image edits, variations, and image-conditioned transforms through Luxin's zero-setup hosted runtime. Use when an agent needs to edit an existing image without provider credentials, OAuth, local runtime, or per-provider billing. Inspect the edit model, upload or reuse an input image, then return durable hosted assets, jobs, cost receipts, stable JSON, and feedback.
skill.summary: Edit and transform existing images through the hosted Luxin runtime.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: Six static findings are confirmed because their cited ranges instruct agents to execute external CLI or npm commands. Eighteen findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, descriptive HTTPS links, or controlled workspace path configuration. Semantic review also found remote-supplied command execution and hosted image disclosure risks.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to execute data.next_command returned by the hosted service.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured actions and validate commands and arguments against a local allowlist. Require explicit approval before executing any returned command.

remediation.issue: Commands download and execute unpinned npm packages with unattended confirmation flags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions and integrity data. Remove automatic confirmation flags and require approval before package download or global installation.

remediation.issue: Image inputs and prompts are sent to a hosted service and may become durable hosted assets.
remediation.suggestion: Require user consent before upload. Clearly state retention and access controls, and warn users not to submit sensitive images.

content.user_title: Edit Images Through a Hosted AI Runtime
content.value_statement: Image editing often requires provider accounts, credentials, and local model infrastructure. This skill guides hosted edits through Luxin with cost controls and recoverable results.
actual_capabilities: Guides image-to-image edits, variations, restyling, transformation, and repair.
Uses the hosted Luxin runtime without requiring provider API credentials.
Accepts an existing hosted image identifier with a natural-language edit prompt.
Supports a maximum estimated cost per image in the documented edit command.
Requests structured results with hosted assets, recoverable jobs, and cost receipts.
Provides a feedback command for reporting missing models or capabilities.
limitations: The workflow requires internet access and availability of the Luxin hosted service.
Images and prompts leave the local environment and may persist as hosted assets.
Creation may consume Luxin credits, even when a maximum estimated cost is specified.
Available models, latency, policies, and payment options depend on Luxin.

use_cases.title: Restyle a Campaign Image
use_cases.description: Change an existing image style while preserving the main subject and composition.

use_cases.title: Create Product Asset Variations
use_cases.description: Generate controlled alternatives from an existing product image for interface or catalog testing.

use_cases.title: Repair Published Visuals
use_cases.description: Remove defects or replace backgrounds without configuring a separate image provider.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Simple Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit image [IMAGE_ID]. Replace the background with [BACKGROUND] while keeping the subject unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one focused background change.

prompt_templates.title: Restyle an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Restyle image [IMAGE_ID] as [STYLE]. Preserve the subject, pose, framing, and important text.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants a visual style change with clear preservation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Repair With Detailed Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Repair image [IMAGE_ID]. Fix [DEFECTS], preserve [REQUIRED_DETAILS], avoid [UNWANTED_CHANGES], and keep the original dimensions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A production asset needs precise repairs and exclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Hosted Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the edit model for image [IMAGE_ID]. Estimate cost, require approval before spending, apply [EDIT], and return the asset link and receipt.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs model inspection, cost control, and recoverable output.

output_examples.input: Replace the office background in image_123 with a bright studio. Keep the person and clothing unchanged.
output_examples.output: The edited image is available at the hosted asset link. The subject remains unchanged, and the background is now a bright studio.

output_examples.input: Repair scratches in image_456 and preserve its original colors and dimensions.
output: The scratches were repaired while retaining the original color treatment.
The output dimensions match the source image.
A hosted asset link and cost receipt are available.

best_practices: State exactly what must change and what must remain unchanged.
Review estimated cost and require approval before any paid creation step.
Use non-sensitive images and confirm hosted retention terms before upload.
anti_patterns: Do not upload confidential images without permission and an approved retention policy.
Do not execute service-provided commands without validating their command and arguments.
Do not use vague prompts when identity, text, dimensions, or composition must remain stable.

faq.question: Does this skill require an image provider API key?
faq.answer: No provider API key is required. The workflow uses a hosted Luxin identity and credit balance.

faq.question: Can it edit a local image path directly?
faq.answer: The documented edit command expects a Luxin image identifier. Upload or reuse an input image before editing.

faq.question: Can an edit cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. Creation may consume Luxin credits, and the command supports a maximum estimated cost per image.

faq.question: Where are edited images stored?
faq.answer: The skill describes durable hosted media URLs. Review Luxin retention and access terms before using sensitive content.

faq.question: Which edit model does the example use?
faq.answer: The examples use openai.gpt-image-2-edit through the Luxin CLI.

faq.question: What happens when Luxin lacks a required capability?
faq.answer: Use a fallback only for the missing capability. The skill also documents a feedback command for reporting the gap.
